newsitem.title: UK: UK digital TV group in tie-up talks with BT.
newsitem.headline: UK digital TV group in tie-up talks with BT.

text.p: British Digital Broadcasting (BDB), a consortium of UK television giants, has begun talks about an alliance with British Telecommunications, the Times said on Wednesday.

The newspaper said BDB, formed recently to bid for licences to broadcast digital terrestrial television in the UK, had asked BT to devise interactive set-top boxes that could also be used for home banking and shopping.
BT would share the revenue generated by these services in exchange for subsidising the retail price of the boxes, the Times said.
BDB was formed earlier this year by British Sky Broadcasting and ITV companies Carlton Communications and Granada Group.
The group has bid for licences to operate up to three "multiplexes", multi-channel digital frequencies, from UK broadcasting regulator Independent Television Commission.
BDB will learn next month whether it has won the licence to start digital terrestrial television which will give viewers the choice of more than 200 channels when it is launched by early 1998.
Digital compression improves sound and picture quality and the technology permits a link to interactive services.
BDB's only rival in the licence bid is Digital Television Network, controlled by International Cable Tel, the U.S. cable group.
